findings.title: READY read and GATE_SUBMITTED_ONCE write do not atomically consume the one-shot grant
findings.requirement: The request permits maximum_attempts=1 and excludes a second fixture; the recorder explicitly claims a single gate and one-shot admission.
findings.mechanism: Two invocations can both validate the same grant and read COPY_INSTALLED_ATTESTED_READY_FOR_SINGLE_GATE before either writes. Each retains its own READY snapshot. write_registry uses O_EXCL only for a temporary pathname, which os.replace removes; after the first replacement the second stale writer can create the temporary file again and successfully overwrite the registry. There is no durable exclusive claim or locked compare-and-set before prove_private_fixture. Both invocations can therefore enter the existing provisioning owner. The later manifest callback is too late to prevent a second fixture from starting.

reproducer.expected: At most one entry to the existing prove_private_fixture under one bound grant.
reproducer.observed: Real require_grant accepted the same valid synthetic request/grant twice; both observed READY. Real main and real write_registry then admitted two test-model-projection-pg owner entries, each with 900 seconds. No exception in either invocation; all test threads joined. The final assertion failed because 2 != 1.
reproducer.substitutions: Authority reads use synthetic in-memory effects/grant/request data; test metadata and paths are private scratch. A barrier selects the valid concurrent interleaving and serializes actual file replacements. Only runpy's owner entry and signal registration are substituted in this reproducer. The existing owner entry is a no-effect sentinel, not OCI/DB. The barriers do not change grant validation or the recorder state predicate.
reproducer.control: The ordinary single-call metadata path succeeds and the same recorder rejects a sequential second call after its state was consumed. The failure is concurrent admission, not a permanently invalid grant or an always-failing observer.

findings.minimal_remedy: Add a retained per-attempt/per-nonce exclusive consumed marker using O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, or hold a local lock while re-reading READY and durably consuming it. Acquire the claim after validation and before any owner call; preserve it on every outcome and refuse reuse. Keep the existing owner, family, attestor and cleanup untouched. Reproduce in the parent, verify one ordinary positive plus concurrent/sequential refusal, rebind runtime-copy/source/request hashes as needed, and request focused re-review. No new lifecycle framework is necessary.
findings.impact_limit: Demonstrated SOURCE admission to a substituted existing-owner entry under a controlled valid interleaving. This is not a physical double-provision observation, an arbitrary-actor privilege escalation, or a model/provider bypass. No real grant existed and none was exercised. An external serialized coordinator is operational mitigation but does not make this recorder's advertised one-shot check atomic.

Reader calls ModelDispatch.read using persisted owner/run/binding/approval/projection refs and validates the qualified payload through the adapter. The qualified reader is inside _read, so it executes in the second process, not merely a second call in the producer. The existing fixture CLI helper chooses installed -I -B -m execution when OMNIS_B06B_INSTALLED=1.

recorder_review.grant: Real current require_grant refuses immediately with holder=null. A positive synthetic grant and 12 selected invalid holder/SID/nonce/request hash/grant hash/root/target/deadline variants were exercised; recorder-hash and inode divergence were separately refused. These selected negatives are not an exhaustive hostile-JSON schema certification.
recorder_review.source_artifact_paths: main requires manifest location/hash, rejects absolute/traversal and named protected input paths, verifies canonical source bytes and canonical artifacts contained in ATTEMPT, and validates the registered root dev/ino/uid/mode before entering the owner. Source-manifest/artifact mutation tests refused before the owner. The real attempt has not reached prepared state: source-manifest completeness, source-to-wheel-to-installed provenance, the full module inventory and artifact hashes still must be populated and attested by the parent before any separate grant/effect. No missing future artifact is credited as verified.
recorder_review.namespace: The wrapper patches namespace['prove_private_fixture'].__globals__ rather than runpy's returned dict alone. A test with a distinct returned dictionary exercises the real source owner body with every Docker/DB/process/attestation effect seam substituted. The original manifest writer is called, four filesystem identities and the original manifest hash are recorded, then the existing attestor seam and gate seam are reached. Thus the interception is on the callable's actual globals.
recorder_review.ddl_frontier: The recording is before the existing gate and installed application migration/DDL (owner lines 974-988), but after PostgreSQL provision/init/readiness. It must not be described as preceding the container's own initdb.
recorder_review.failure_cleanup_independence: Injected callback metadata OSError and callback grant expiry prevent the gate seam and still invoke the existing cleanup seam. Injected final registry failure occurs after that cleanup and does not fabricate a successful readback. The wrapper has no cleanup implementation and leaves GATE_EXITED_READBACK_PENDING for the parent's independent readback, not VERIFIED. These are SOURCE tests of owner control flow, not physical cleanup proof.

finding_dispositions.reason: After validating the grant, READY state, environment, source and artifact hashes, main atomically creates a per-nonce retained marker with O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW and mode 0600. A second valid READY reader loses at that open before any owner entry. Marker content is flushed/fsynced, then the attempt directory is fsynced before registry submission and owner invocation. No deletion or rearm path was added.
